_about: Curated planetary targets for the REAL bundle (Phase 3). Every feature has a status, the value actually used, a citation and a caveat. basisValue is in the feature's Earth units (degC, mm/yr) and is normalized with the same fixed Earth bounds as the sites; clipping is recorded by build_bundle.py. status 'unavailable' => null => excluded from similarity. Sources gathered 2026-11-13; see docs/methodology.md.

targets.name: Jezero Crater — Perseverance landing site

coord.source: Zafrir et al. 2026, Icarus 460, 117296 (doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2026.117296): Perseverance landed at 18.44 N, 77.45 E
coord.note: Secondary citation; Octavia E. Butler Landing. Values below are from MEDA along the early rover traverse, not one fixed point.

targets.summary: Crater-floor lava flows (Máaz/Séítah) beside an ancient lake delta with clays and carbonates; Perseverance landing site.

terrain.note: No published relief for a 10 x 10 km window; needs MOLA/HiRISE DEM processing with the same method as Earth (planned).

aridity.citation: NASA Science, Mars Facts: "the Martian atmosphere is too thin for liquid water to exist for long on the surface"
aridity.note: Physical constraint, not a measurement; the page does not discuss precipitation explicitly.

temp.display: ≈ −52 °C (midpoint of daily-mean surface temperature 210–232 K over one Mars year)
temp.citation: Munguira et al. 2024, JGR Planets 129, e2024JE008385 — One Martian Year of Near-Surface Temperatures at Jezero From MEDA (results, Fig. 4a)
temp.note: No annual mean is published; we use the midpoint of the published range (derived). Normalized value could lie anywhere from 0 to 0.20 across that range.

temp_range.citation: Munguira et al. 2023, JGR Planets 128, e2022JE007559 — Near Surface Atmospheric Temperatures at Jezero From MEDA (conclusions; table: 81 K at Ls 25°, 104 K at Ls 180°)
temp_range.note: Uses the lower end of the published range; every value in the range exceeds Earth's bound (35 °C) and clips to 1. Coverage Ls 13–203° only.

veg.citation: NASA Science, Mars Facts: "Scientists don't expect to find living things currently thriving on Mars."
veg.note: NDVI is not defined for Mars; treated as NDVI 0 (bare).

geology.display: Basaltic lava flows (Máaz formation) on the crater floor
geology.citation: Sun et al. 2023, JGR Planets 128, e2022JE007613 (§1, §2.2.2); Farley et al. 2022, Science 377, eabo2196
geology.note: Applies to the landing site. The delta (not the landing site) hosts Fe/Mg clays and carbonates; it would map to 'clay'.

ice.display: No near-surface ice expected at 18° N
ice.citation: Piqueux et al. 2019, GRL 46, 14290 — shallow ice consistent with latitudes as low as 35° N / 45° S
ice.note: Inference from the latitude limit; no Jezero-specific statement found.

targets.name: Lunar South Pole — Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge (Artemis)

coord.source: NASA ACD-50044 Rev A, Lunar Surface Data Book (2023), Fig. 7.3.1: point C1 (89.468° S, 222.6° E) on the Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge
coord.note: 222.6° E converted to −137.4°. Point definitions (C1/C2) differ between papers.

targets.summary: Sunlit ridge near Shackleton crater in the Artemis exploration zone; anorthositic highlands next to permanently shadowed cold traps that hold water ice.

terrain.note: No published relief for a 10 x 10 km window; needs LOLA DEM processing with the same method as Earth (planned). Shackleton is 4.2 km deep (rim to floor), which is not this metric.

aridity.citation: NASA Science, Moon Facts: "The Moon's weak atmosphere and its lack of liquid water cannot support life as we know it."

temp.display: ≈ 200 K (−73 °C) in summer, colder in winter
temp.citation: Williams et al. 2019, JGR Planets 124, 2505 — Seasonal Polar Temperatures on the Moon (Diviner; text on Fig. 10d, Connecting Ridge)
temp.note: No annual mean is published. Summer ≈200 K is an upper bound, so the annual mean is below Earth's coldest bound (−60 °C) and clips to 0 whatever its exact value.

temp_range.note: No published day–night range for the ridge; at the pole, season and shadowing dominate over a simple diurnal cycle.

veg.citation: NASA Science, Moon Facts (no liquid water, cannot support life as we know it)
veg.note: NDVI is not defined for the Moon; treated as NDVI 0 (bare).

geology.display: Anorthosite (feldspathic highlands; regolith and breccia at the surface)
geology.citation: Patterson et al. 2024, JGR Planets 129, e2023JE008275 — Lithologies and Chronologic Opportunities of Materials to Be Returned From the Artemis Exploration Zone
geology.note: Interpretation from orbital data; surface is impact-processed regolith, possibly with South Pole–Aitken ejecta.

ice.display: Water ice in nearby permanently shadowed regions
ice.citation: Colaprete et al. 2010, Science 330, 463 (LCROSS: 5.6 ± 2.9 wt% water ice in Cabeus); Li et al. 2018, PNAS 115, 8907 (M3: surface-exposed ice in polar cold traps)
ice.note: Region-level: ice is in cold traps (Cabeus is ~100 km away), not on the sunlit ridge surface itself.
